title: Module inputs and outputs
description: Find every current module's input data, saved outputs, upstream producers and downstream consumers, including tools nested inside a Home module.
objectives: Choose a starting module from the data you already have.
Identify what each module reads and writes.
Follow the linked module lessons and API contracts for the next step.
prerequisite: Install spaCR and open Home. This lesson explains navigation and data handoffs; the linked module lessons provide the worked data examples. Inputs and outputs include conditional alternatives, as explained for each module.

scenes.narration: Choose a module by the data you have and the result you need. Home shows the main modules; related tools can open inside a parent. This chapter-by-chapter reference covers every current route. Inputs and outputs can be conditional: an image classifier and a feature classifier need different data, and a viewer does not automatically save everything it displays. The notes for each module explain those differences. Keep the original files and use the recorded object, plate and well identities when passing results between modules.

Open Mask from Home. Select channels and models, inspect a preview, then run Mask. Measure consumes the merged arrays; the counts database is not yet a feature table. Input data: Microscope images; Segmentation checkpoint. Microscope images: Source image folder; original files, supported vendor files or imported TIFFs. Segmentation checkpoint: Saved Cellpose-compatible checkpoint or a compatible installed backend selected with its own configuration. Output data: Images and label masks; Label masks; Object counts. Images and label masks: merged/*.npy in the project; channels and integer label planes share each field array. Label masks: masks/ when retained, or explicitly saved image/mask pairs. Intermediate masks may be removed by cleanup. Object counts: measurements/measurements.db; Mask counts alone are not per-object feature measurements. Mask to Measure: Use the same project and the correct image/mask channel indices. Cellpose Workbench to Mask: Select the saved compatible checkpoint in Mask. Import Images to Mask: Use imported image planes and identities; image-only imports still need segmentation. Format Converter to Mask: Use the converted layout and preserve source identity mappings. Mask to Timelapse: Enable the nested time-series route before generating linked labels.

Open Measure from Home. Measure reads images and label planes together. Enable crop saving if you need PNG files; keep the database and source project together for streamed crops. Input data: Images and label masks; Label masks. Output data: Measured objects; Object crops. Measured objects: measurements/measurements.db; object tables depend on the enabled cell, nucleus, pathogen and organelle masks. Relevant tables depend on the selected route: cell, nucleus, pathogen, cytoplasm. Relevant columns depend on the selected route: plateID, rowID, columnID, fieldID. Object crops: data/**/*_png when save_png is enabled; png_list indexes saved crops. Supported workflows can instead stream crops from merged arrays and masks. Relevant tables depend on the selected route: png_list. Relevant columns depend on the selected route: png_path, prcfo. Mask to Measure: Use the same project and the correct image/mask channel indices. Measure to Annotate: Save or stream crops with stable object identities. Measure to Classify: Choose the image or tabular family to match your input. Make Masks to Measure: Use FEATURES to pair images and masks and write a measured project; standalone masks are not merged arrays. External Masks to Measure: Re-measure only when needed; External Masks can already perform measurement. Measure to Image UMAP: Choose feature columns and inspect representative crops. Measure to Embeddings: Retain encoder and channel-policy provenance. Measure to Gate Editor: Use the actual measured feature definitions and units. Measure to Graph Builder: Choose explicit variables, groups and filters. Measure to QC: Review available checks and missing evidence. Measure to Recruitment: Require the intended compartment intensities and identities. Measure to Invasion Assay: Require two-colour stain measurements and appropriate baseline controls. Measure to Replication Assay: Require explicit parasite-to-vacuole identities. Timelapse to Measure: Use the time-series project with stable frame/object identities. Measure to Motility Assay: Combine measured objects with matching tracks. Measure to Feature Explorer: Define the class comparison and inspect filtering. Measure to Database Browser: Inspect actual tables before exporting. Measure to AnnData Export: Export compatible feature and metadata columns. Measure to Dose–Response: Join the measured response to explicit doses and controls.

Open Annotate from Home. Label representative objects in png_list before supervised training. Use separate annotations for different questions and keep training and evaluation groups independent. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops; Reusable gates. Reusable gates: Saved threshold/polygon gate definitions or a selected object set; apply a gate to the same feature definitions. Output data: Training annotations. Training annotations: A chosen annotation column in measurements/measurements.db, table png_list; labels belong to object identities. Relevant tables depend on the selected route: png_list. Relevant columns depend on the selected route: prcfo. Measure to Annotate: Save or stream crops with stable object identities. Annotate to Classify: Keep labelled training and evaluation groups separate. External Masks to Annotate: Keep the newly measured project and crop index together. Import to Annotate: Imported tables require explicit column and object-identity mappings. Gate Editor to Annotate: Apply compatible gates, then review candidate labels. Annotate to Annotator Agreement: Choose independent annotation columns for the same objects.

Open Classify from Home. Choose Computer Vision for crops or streamed object images, or Tabular Machine Learning for measured feature columns. The two families consume different inputs. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops; Training annotations. Output data: Object classification scores; Trained image classifier; Fitted feature classifier; Classifier evaluation bundle. Object classification scores: Saved score CSVs and, when merged, measurements/measurements.db, table png_list. Relevant tables depend on the selected route: png_list. Relevant columns depend on the selected route: pred, cv_predictions, ml_pred, predictions. Trained image classifier: Saved classifier checkpoint, model settings and matching channel/preprocessing configuration. Fitted feature classifier: The fitted tabular classifier and its recorded feature list, training settings and validation results. Classifier evaluation bundle: Held-out predictions, labels, split metadata and calibration/leakage metrics for a saved classifier run. Measure to Classify: Choose the image or tabular family to match your input. Annotate to Classify: Keep labelled training and evaluation groups separate. Classify to Regression: Select the intended CV or ML score column and preserve plate/well identity. Classify to Classifier Evaluation: Use the matching held-out predictions and split metadata. Classify to Activation: Also provide the matching crops and channel preprocessing. Classify to Explain CV Model: Select CV predictions and the matching measured objects.

Open Map Barcodes from Home. Supply the references that encode your experiment. Inspect mapped counts and barcode QC before pairing well-level guide counts with phenotype scores. Input data: Sequencing reads. Sequencing reads: Single-end or paired FASTQ files, with the matching barcode reference tables. Output data: Guide counts per well. Guide counts per well: Map Barcodes run folder: unique_combinations.csv and annotated_reads.h5. Well identity requires the corresponding barcode references. Relevant columns depend on the selected route: count. Map Barcodes to Regression: Pair guide counts with phenotype scores using consistent plate/well keys. Map Barcodes to Barcode QC: Check mapping and coverage before guide filtering.

Open Regression from Home. Match plate and well identifiers across phenotype and guide-count inputs, select the response and controls, and inspect diagnostics before interpreting hits. Direct measured responses are also supported. Input data: Object classification scores; Guide counts per well; Optical barcode assignments; Measured objects. Optical barcode assignments: OPS destination measurements.db: per-well geometry, phenotype alignment, nuclei and barcode tables; optional per-cycle reads. Relevant tables depend on the selected route: ops_geometry, ops_phenotype, ops_objects, ops_barcodes, ops_reads. Output data: Regression results and hits. Regression results and hits: Selected run results folder: coefficient/result CSVs, hit tables, settings and diagnostic figures. Classify to Regression: Select the intended CV or ML score column and preserve plate/well identity. Map Barcodes to Regression: Pair guide counts with phenotype scores using consistent plate/well keys. OPS to Regression: Join/aggregate decoded objects to phenotype and guide inputs explicitly before Regression; this is not a direct CSV handoff. Regression to Run Compare: Compare compatible saved result sets and their settings. Regression to Hit List: Inspect ranked hits and guide agreement. Regression to Volcano Explorer: Inspect saved effects and adjusted significance. Regression to Diagnostics: Open the diagnostics actually written by this run. Regression to Methods & Results: Review exported prose and every traced result. Regression to Investigate Hit: Join compatible phenotype and object data for the chosen hit.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Feature Explorer. Rank measured features for a chosen class comparison; review filtering and class definitions before interpreting the ranking. Input data: Measured objects; Training annotations. Output data: Figures and table exports. Figures and table exports: The output location chosen by the tool; exports describe the selected data and filters. Measure to Feature Explorer: Define the class comparison and inspect filtering.

Open Import from Home, then choose Format Converter. Convert supported microscope formats to a configured TIFF layout while preserving source mappings. Conversion does not generate object measurements. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Microscope images. Format Converter to Mask: Use the converted layout and preserve source identity mappings.

Open Import from Home. Import external measurements with explicit object/column mappings, or choose Import Images, Format Converter or External Masks. Imported measurements are not a fresh Measure run. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks; External measurements. External measurements: Third-party measurement CSV/database tables and their image, mask and object-identity mappings. Output data: Measured objects; Object crops. Import to Annotate: Imported tables require explicit column and object-identity mappings.

Open Import from Home, then choose External Masks. Assign corresponding images and existing integer label masks, then create and measure a spaCR project without rerunning segmentation. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Images and label masks; Measured objects; Object crops. External Masks to Measure: Re-measure only when needed; External Masks can already perform measurement. External Masks to Annotate: Keep the newly measured project and crop index together.

Find Plate Queue in the application's Help or tools menus. Run the chosen pipeline across plates. Outputs are those of each queued module; retain each plate and its settings separately. Input data: Run queue. Run queue: Saved module/plate/settings job definitions and dependency order. Output data: Run history and artifacts. Run history and artifacts: Project run records, settings, output paths, artifact provenance, status and logs.

Find Batch Runner in the application's Help or tools menus. Validate and execute module jobs in dependency order. Each job writes its own module outputs and log. Input data: Run queue. Output data: Run history and artifacts.

Find Distributed Jobs in the application's Help or tools menus. Submit a configured run to a remote execution target and inspect its status and logs. Retrieve the actual module artifacts before downstream analysis. Input data: Run queue. Output data: Run history and artifacts.

Find Database Browser in the application's Help or tools menus. Browse selected tables and export rows; table inspection does not rerun image analysis. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports. Measure to Database Browser: Inspect actual tables before exporting.

Find Run History in the application's Help or tools menus. Inspect saved run status, settings, outputs and logs; a completed run does not establish biological validity. Input data: Run history and artifacts. Output data: Run history and artifacts.

Find Report in the application's Help or tools menus. Package recorded results, settings and QC into a shareable report without silently rerunning the analysis. Input data: Run history and artifacts; Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Quality-control results: Stored project checks and QC reports; a missing check is not a passing result. Output data: Shareable reports. Shareable reports: Exported HTML/PDF or methods/results documents derived from recorded analysis outputs.

Find Data Manager in the application's Help or tools menus. Inspect project files and disk usage. Removing derived artifacts invalidates downstream uses of those files; original images must remain recoverable. Input data: Run history and artifacts. Output data: Run history and artifacts.

Find Pipeline Graph in the application's Help or tools menus. Read recorded artifact dependencies and stale/missing status. The graph describes provenance and does not regenerate missing artifacts. Input data: Run history and artifacts. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open QC from Home. Inspect stored segmentation, unit, leakage and plate-effect checks. Open its nested viewers for detailed inspection. Input data: Measured objects; Quality-control results. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Measure to QC: Review available checks and missing evidence.

Open Database Browser from Home, then choose Lineage. Inspect recorded cell/nucleus/pathogen/organelle containment links; this is object containment, not time-series lineage inference. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Experiment Design from Home. Enter conditions, controls, replicates and plate constraints, then export the experimental layout before acquisition. Input data: Screen design and power estimates. Screen design and power estimates: Saved planning tables or figures based on explicitly chosen effect sizes, variability and sampling assumptions. Output data: Experimental layout. Experimental layout: Exported plate/condition/control/replicate map. Keep its plate and well identifiers consistent with the acquired data. Experiment Design to Power / Design: Use the experimental layout to define sampling assumptions, then revise the design. Experiment Design to Dose–Response: Acquire and measure the experiment first, preserving dose/condition identities.

Open QC from Home, then choose Layer Viewer. Inspect aligned image, label and point/ROI layers for the selected field. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Power / Design from Home. Estimate sampling needs from chosen effect sizes and variability; pilot measurements are optional evidence for assumptions. Input data: Screen design and power estimates; Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Screen design and power estimates. Experiment Design to Power / Design: Use the experimental layout to define sampling assumptions, then revise the design.

Open Run Compare from Home. Compare compatible saved settings, counts and hit lists without treating changed input data as a controlled model comparison. Input data: Run history and artifacts; Regression results and hits. Output data: Run/model comparison. Run/model comparison: Comparison tables and figures from compatible saved runs or masks; agreement is not ground-truth accuracy. Regression to Run Compare: Compare compatible saved result sets and their settings.

Open Database Browser from Home, then choose Tabulate. Choose grouping variables and measurement columns, then inspect pivot tables and groupwise sample sizes. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Dose–Response from Home. Supply dose and response columns, controls and units before curve fitting; this route does not require sequencing. Input data: Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Assay results; Figures and table exports. Assay results: Assay-specific result tables and figures in the configured destination, preserving well and condition identities. Experiment Design to Dose–Response: Acquire and measure the experiment first, preserving dose/condition identities. Measure to Dose–Response: Join the measured response to explicit doses and controls.

Find Project Browser in the application's Help or tools menus. Locate projects and inspect their stage, last run, disk use and stale outputs. Input data: Run history and artifacts. Output data: Run history and artifacts.

Open QC from Home, then choose Outliers. Review robust object/well outlier scores and the selected exclusion rule before carrying filtered data into analysis. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports.

Open Embeddings from Home. Encode object images with a chosen model and channel policy. Retain object identities and encoder provenance when supplying the features to downstream exploration. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops. Output data: Image embeddings. Image embeddings: Object-indexed encoder features, with channel policy and encoder provenance. The encoding API returns features; persistence is caller-dependent. Measure to Embeddings: Retain encoder and channel-policy provenance. Embeddings to Image UMAP: Supply the encoder feature table with matching object IDs; do not assume every GUI route automatically persists it.

Open QC from Home, then choose Control Charts. Compare designated controls across plates and inspect drift; the definition of a control comes from the experiment. Input data: Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Training Runs. Compare saved training histories, metrics and settings from compatible model runs. Input data: Run history and artifacts. Output data: Run/model comparison.

Open Align & Stitch from Home. Inspect tile geometry, overlap and channel mapping, then save the mosaic with coordinate records. OPS also needs the original cycle/site identities. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Aligned mosaic and coordinates. Aligned mosaic and coordinates: Align & Stitch destination: composed image and the tile-coordinate/layout records needed to interpret it. Align & Stitch to OPS: Carry tile coordinates and original sequencing cycles into OPS; a flattened mosaic alone is insufficient.

Open Make Masks from Home. Curate image/mask pairs for segmentation training, or use FEATURES to assign images and masks and invoke measurement. Saving a mask does not train a classifier. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Curated training fields; Label masks. Curated training fields: Separate image and integer-mask files with matching field identities; preserve original images and labels. Make Masks to Cellpose Workbench: Use independently checked image/mask pairs. Make Masks to Measure: Use FEATURES to pair images and masks and write a measured project; standalone masks are not merged arrays. Make Masks to Plaque Assay: Use plaque masks with matching source images; cell masks are not automatically plaque labels.

Open Graph Builder from Home, then choose Plate Viewer. Aggregate the selected measurement by well and inspect plate patterns and controls. Input data: Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Image UMAP from Home. Project measured features or supplied encoder features and inspect representative crops. A cluster is a candidate grouping, not a validated phenotype. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops; Image embeddings. Output data: Projection and clusters. Projection and clusters: Image UMAP/PCA coordinate tables, selected clusters and figures for the loaded measurement data. Measure to Image UMAP: Choose feature columns and inspect representative crops. Embeddings to Image UMAP: Supply the encoder feature table with matching object IDs; do not assume every GUI route automatically persists it. Image UMAP to Gate Editor: Supply the matching coordinate/feature columns when defining a selection.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Prediction Profiler. Inspect how a fitted model responds as an input feature changes; predictions do not establish causal effects. Input data: Fitted feature classifier. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Graph Builder from Home. Choose variables, groups and plotting settings from the loaded table, then export the figure with its analysis context. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports. Measure to Graph Builder: Choose explicit variables, groups and filters.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Investigate Hit. Link a regression hit to candidate objects and quantitative well-level evidence. This does not independently validate the hit. Input data: Regression results and hits; Object classification scores; Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports. Regression to Investigate Hit: Join compatible phenotype and object data for the chosen hit.

Open Gate Editor from Home. Define threshold or polygon gates on actual feature/coordinate columns, then apply the saved gate to compatible objects. Input data: Measured objects; Projection and clusters. Output data: Reusable gates. Image UMAP to Gate Editor: Supply the matching coordinate/feature columns when defining a selection. Gate Editor to Annotate: Apply compatible gates, then review candidate labels. Measure to Gate Editor: Use the actual measured feature definitions and units.

Find Feature Dictionary in the application's Help or tools menus. Look up feature definitions and units before choosing measurement columns. Input data: Feature definitions. Feature definitions: The installed feature dictionary; definitions describe existing measurements and do not compute them. Output data: Feature definitions.

Open Graph Builder from Home, then choose Small Multiples. Compare groups in small-multiple plots with explicit shared or independent axes. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Plaque Assay from Home. Analyse plaque images or existing masks with the configured plaque model. This route need not pass through Measure; use the dedicated plaque example. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Assay results; Label masks. Make Masks to Plaque Assay: Use plaque masks with matching source images; cell masks are not automatically plaque labels.

Open Recruitment from Home. Use compartment intensity measurements and matching host/pathogen identities to compute recruitment ratios. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Assay results. Measure to Recruitment: Require the intended compartment intensities and identities.

Open Invasion Assay from Home. Use the required two-colour differential-staining measurements and stain-baseline controls to distinguish attachment from invasion. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Assay results. Measure to Invasion Assay: Require two-colour stain measurements and appropriate baseline controls.

Open Replication Assay from Home. Count parasites using explicit vacuole identity and compare condition distributions; host identity alone does not define a vacuole. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Assay results. Measure to Replication Assay: Require explicit parasite-to-vacuole identities.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Cellpose Workbench. Open Cellpose Workbench inside Make Masks and train from verified image/mask pairs. Evaluate on separate fields before selecting the checkpoint in Mask. Input data: Curated training fields. Output data: Segmentation checkpoint. Make Masks to Cellpose Workbench: Use independently checked image/mask pairs. Cellpose Workbench to Mask: Select the saved compatible checkpoint in Mask.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Mask the whole folder. Apply the selected segmentation model to the open image folder through Make Masks; inspect saved labels before measuring them. Input data: Microscope images; Segmentation checkpoint. Output data: Label masks.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Model Compare. Compare model masks on identical fields. Without independent reference labels, agreement does not measure segmentation accuracy. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks; Segmentation checkpoint. Output data: Run/model comparison.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Model Zoo. Inspect model provenance and download/install compatible checkpoints or backends. A listed backend is not itself a checkpoint file. Input data: Segmentation checkpoint. Output data: Segmentation checkpoint.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Curate. Correct labels and track assignments while retaining a record of the edits. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks; Linked time-series objects. Linked time-series objects: Tracked labels and frame/object associations from the time-series project, with frame interval and units. Output data: Label masks; Linked time-series objects.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Napari Bridge. Send the matching image/labels to napari and import the revised labels back with field identity preserved. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Label masks.

Open Import from Home, then choose Import Images. Review field identities, image channels and optional external masks before writing a separate project. Image-only imports still need segmentation before measurement. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Microscope images; Images and label masks; Label masks. Import Images to Mask: Use imported image planes and identities; image-only imports still need segmentation.

Open Map Barcodes from Home, then choose Barcode QC. Inspect mapping depth, coverage, collisions and positional effects before guide-count filtering. Input data: Guide counts per well. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Map Barcodes to Barcode QC: Check mapping and coverage before guide filtering.

Open Image UMAP from Home, then choose Image Scatter. Plot selected measurement columns with object-crop inspection. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops. Output data: Projection and clusters; Figures and table exports.

Open Image UMAP from Home, then choose PCA. Inspect principal components and feature loadings for the selected measured objects. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Projection and clusters; Figures and table exports.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Volcano Explorer. Open a saved regression result and inspect effect sizes, adjusted significance and individual hit records. Input data: Regression results and hits. Output data: Figures and table exports. Regression to Volcano Explorer: Inspect saved effects and adjusted significance.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Hit List. Filter and rank saved hits with their effects, FDR and guide agreement. Input data: Regression results and hits. Output data: Figures and table exports. Regression to Hit List: Inspect ranked hits and guide agreement.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Methods & Results. Draft methods/results text from recorded settings and results; review every claim before publication. Input data: Run history and artifacts; Regression results and hits. Output data: Shareable reports. Regression to Methods & Results: Review exported prose and every traced result.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Diagnostics. Inspect the diagnostic panels saved by the chosen regression run; distinguish missing diagnostics from passed assumptions. Input data: Regression results and hits. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Regression to Diagnostics: Open the diagnostics actually written by this run.

Open Measure from Home, then choose Illumination. Estimate and apply flat-field correction at configured stages. Keep corrected display values distinct from raw measurements and record the applied policy. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Microscope images.

Open Measure from Home, then choose AnnData Export. Export an AnnData .h5ad file with object metadata and measured features for downstream single-cell analysis. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: AnnData export. AnnData export: An exported .h5ad file containing measured features and object metadata. Measure to AnnData Export: Export compatible feature and metadata columns.

Open Measure from Home, then choose Motility Assay. Inspect track speed and infection-related measurements with an explicit frame interval and pixel calibration. Input data: Linked time-series objects; Measured objects. Output data: Assay results; Figures and table exports. Timelapse to Motility Assay: Supply frame interval and pixel calibration. Measure to Motility Assay: Combine measured objects with matching tracks.

Open Mask from Home, then choose Timelapse. Open Timelapse within Mask to segment and link objects across ordered frames; inspect links before downstream motility analysis. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Images and label masks; Label masks; Linked time-series objects. Mask to Timelapse: Enable the nested time-series route before generating linked labels. Timelapse to Measure: Use the time-series project with stable frame/object identities. Timelapse to Motility Assay: Supply frame interval and pixel calibration.

Open Mask from Home, then choose OPS. Use sequencing-cycle images and phenotype alignment to decode barcodes per nucleus. Aggregate/join the decoded identities to compatible phenotype inputs before Regression; the OPS database is not a drop-in FASTQ count CSV. Input data: Microscope images; Aligned mosaic and coordinates. Output data: Optical barcode assignments. Align & Stitch to OPS: Carry tile coordinates and original sequencing cycles into OPS; a flattened mosaic alone is insufficient. OPS to Regression: Join/aggregate decoded objects to phenotype and guide inputs explicitly before Regression; this is not a direct CSV handoff.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Classifier Evaluation. Inspect held-out predictions, calibration and split/leakage evidence for the matching classifier. Input data: Classifier evaluation bundle. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Classify to Classifier Evaluation: Use the matching held-out predictions and split metadata.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Explain CV Model. Fit a measured-feature surrogate to existing computer-vision scores, preserving identity joins. A surrogate explanation is not causality. Input data: Measured objects; Object classification scores. Output data: Fitted feature classifier; Figures and table exports. Classify to Explain CV Model: Select CV predictions and the matching measured objects.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Activation. Apply the matching image classifier and preprocessing to inspect saliency/model-response maps. Input data: Trained image classifier; Object crops. Output data: Image attribution maps. Image attribution maps: Saved model-response/saliency images for the matching classifier and input preprocessing. Classify to Activation: Also provide the matching crops and channel preprocessing.

Open Annotate from Home, then choose Annotator Agreement. Compare independent annotation columns and inspect discordant objects; agreement is separate from classification accuracy. Input data: Training annotations; Object crops. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Annotate to Annotator Agreement: Choose independent annotation columns for the same objects.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Computer Vision. Train an image classifier from labelled object crops, archives or supported streamed crops. Match channels and preprocessing when applying its checkpoint. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops; Training annotations. Output data: Object classification scores; Trained image classifier; Classifier evaluation bundle.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Tabular Machine Learning. Train a feature-based classifier from measured objects and labels. Inspect missing-feature exclusions and grouped held-out performance before using scores. Input data: Measured objects; Training annotations. Output data: Object classification scores; Fitted feature classifier; Classifier evaluation bundle.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Parameter Sweep. Run explicitly selected regression settings and compare their diagnostics. Keep the input data and evaluation question fixed. Input data: Object classification scores; Guide counts per well. Output data: Run/model comparison; Regression results and hits.

Return to the chapter matching your next data product rather than repeating work you already completed. A count table is not a measured feature table, a projection is not a trained classifier, and a comparison is not a new experiment. The linked API pages carry the same file, table and column contracts, and the specialist lessons demonstrate the individual controls.
